On July 20, 2011, Yao announced his retirement from basketball in a press conference in Shanghai.[[119]](#cite_note-119)[[120]](#cite_note-ap_07202011-120) He cited injuries to his foot and ankle, including the third fracture to his left foot sustained near the end of 2010.[[121]](#cite_note-chron.com-121) His retirement sparked over 1.2 million comments on the Chinese social-networking site [Sina Weibo](/wiki/Sina_Weibo "Sina Weibo").[[122]](#cite_note-122) Reacting to Yao's retirement, NBA commissioner [David Stern](/wiki/David_Stern "David Stern") said Yao was a "bridge between Chinese and American fans" and that he had "a wonderful mixture of talent, dedication, humanitarian aspirations and a sense of humor."[[121]](#cite_note-chron.com-121) Shaquille O'Neal said Yao "was very agile. He could play inside, he could play outside, and if he didn't have those injuries he could've been up there in the top five centers to ever play the game."[[123]](#cite_note-123)

Yao was nominated by a member of the Chinese media for the [Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame](/wiki/Naismith_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame") as a contributor to the game. He would have been eligible for induction as early as 2012, but Yao felt it was too soon and requested that the Hall of Fame delay consideration of the nomination. The Hall granted Yao's request, and said it was Yao's decision when the process would be restarted.[[124]](#cite_note-124)

On September 9, 2016, Yao was inducted into the Hall of Fame along with 4-time NBA champion [Shaquille O'Neal](/wiki/Shaquille_O%27Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") and [Allen Iverson](/wiki/Allen_Iverson "Allen Iverson").[[125]](#cite_note-125) Continuing with the honors, on February 3, 2017, Yao's Number 11 jersey was retired by the Houston Rockets.[[126]](#cite_note-126)

COVID-19 pandemic in China :: part 04 :: chunk_0003
The **COVID-19 pandemic in China** is part of [the worldwide pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of [coronavirus disease 2019](/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") (COVID-19) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). [China](/wiki/China "China") was the first country to experience an outbreak of the disease, the first to impose drastic measures in response (including lockdowns and face mask mandates), and one of the first countries to bring the outbreak under control.

The first wave of the disease manifested as the [2019–2020 COVID-19 outbreak in mainland China](/wiki/2019%E2%80%932020_COVID-19_outbreak_in_mainland_China "2019–2020 COVID-19 outbreak in mainland China"), beginning with a cluster of mysterious [pneumonia](/wiki/Pneumonia "Pneumonia") cases, mostly related to the [Huanan Seafood Market](/wiki/Huanan_Seafood_Wholesale_Market "Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market"), in [Wuhan](/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan"), the capital of [Hubei](/wiki/Hubei "Hubei") province. It was first reported to the local government on 27 December 2019, and published on 31 December. On 8 January 2020, a new [coronavirus](/wiki/Coronavirus "Coronavirus") ([SARS-CoV-2](/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2")) was identified as the cause of the pneumonia by Chinese scientists.[[8]](#cite_note-8) By 29 January, the virus was found to have spread to all [provinces of mainland China](/wiki/Provinces_of_China "Provinces of China").[[9]](#cite_note-:2222-9)[[10]](#cite_note-AllRegions22-10)[[11]](#cite_note-Declared23-11) The virus was first confirmed to have spread to Hong Kong on 23 January 2020, thus originating the [COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Hong_Kong "COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong").[[12]](#cite_note-scmp3047193-12) Confirmed cases were generally transferred to [Princess Margaret Hospital](/wiki/Princess_Margaret_Hospital_(Hong_Kong) "Princess Margaret Hospital (Hong Kong)")'s Infectious Disease Centre

On July 18, 2005, the Rams signed Fitzpatrick to a three-year, $953,000 contract.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Throughout training camp, he competed for a roster spot against [Jeff Smoker](/wiki/Jeff_Smoker "Jeff Smoker") to be the Rams' third-string quarterback. Fitzpatrick was upgraded to the primary backup role in Week 6 after Bulger sustained a shoulder injury and was placed on [injured reserve](/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve").

On November 27, 2005, Fitzpatrick made his professional regular season debut after entering the game in the second quarter against the [Houston Texans](/wiki/2005_Houston_Texans_season "2005 Houston Texans season") to replace injured veteran journeyman [Jamie Martin](/wiki/Jamie_Martin_(American_football) "Jamie Martin (American football)"). For a more comprehensive list, see [List of highest mountains on Earth](/wiki/List_of_highest_mountains_on_Earth "List of highest mountains on Earth").

The summit of Everest is the point at which Earth's surface reaches the greatest distance [above sea level](/wiki/Above_sea_level "Above sea level"). Several other mountains are sometimes claimed to be the "tallest mountains on Earth". [Mauna Kea](/wiki/Mauna_Kea "Mauna Kea") in Hawaii is tallest when measured from its base;[[note 5]](#cite_note-base-55) it rises over 10,200 m (33,464.6 ft) from its base on the mid-ocean floor, but only attains 4,205 m (13,796 ft) above sea level.

By the same measure of base to summit, [Denali](/wiki/Denali "Denali") (also called Mount McKinley) in [Alaska](/wiki/Alaska "Alaska") is taller than Everest as well.[[note 5]](#cite_note-base-55) Despite its height above sea level of only 6,190 m (20,308 ft), Denali sits atop a sloping plain with elevations from 300 to 900 m (980 to 2,950 ft), yielding a height above base in the range of 5,300 to 5,900 m (17,400 to 19,400 ft); a commonly quoted figure is 5,600 m (18,400 ft).[[49]](#cite_note-56)[[50]](#cite_note-57) By comparison, reasonable base elevations for Everest range from 4,200 m (13,800 ft) on the south side to 5,200 m (17,100 ft) on the [Tibetan Plateau](/wiki/Tibetan_Plateau "Tibetan Plateau"), yielding a height above base in the range of 3,650 to 4,650 m (11,980 to 15,260 ft).[[41]](#cite_note-washburn_map-47)

The summit of [Chimborazo](/wiki/Chimborazo "Chimborazo") in [Ecuador](/wiki/Ecuador "Ecuador") is 2,168 m (7,113 ft) farther from Earth's centre (6,384.4 km or 3,967.1 mi) than that of Everest (6,382.3 km, 3,965.8 mi), because the Earth bulges at the equator.[[51]](#cite_note-58) This is despite Chimborazo having a peak of 6,268 m (20,564.3 ft) above sea level versus Mount Everest's 8,848 m (29,028.9 ft).
